# Common Room

A design philosophy for BONDED.

## The idea

A family does not work because people merge. It works because each person stays whole and makes a little space for the others.

Common Room draws that space. Two equal circles, placed at one exact distance, give up a corner each. The square they leave between them is a room that belongs to both.

## Geometry as meaning

Nothing in the mark is decorative. The circles are equal because nobody is ranked. Their centres sit one radius apart on both axes because only at that distance do the corners of the room land exactly where the circles meet.

Move them closer or further and the room disappears. The meaning is carried by the rule, so the rule is never bent.

## Space over shape

The room is always a hole, never a filled shape. Whatever sits behind the mark shows through it: paper, night, a photograph of a day by the sea.

This is the discipline of the whole system. Avatars, patterns, progress and motion are all made by adding people and letting rooms appear between them. Add a person, add a room.

## Quiet, exact, warm

The palette is paper, ink and one warm red called Hearth. The wordmark is lowercase and round, drawn from the same circles as the symbol. There are no gradients, no gloss and no effects, because warmth here comes from restraint, not from decoration.

Motion follows the same logic. Two forms move toward each other, settle, and the room opens. It happens once, in under a second, and never bounces.

## Craft

Every size is drawn for its size. The room opens slightly on dark grounds and at small sizes, and the 16 and 32 pixel favicons are placed on the pixel grid by hand. The symbol overshoots the letters by 2.2 units so it looks as tall as they are.

These corrections are invisible when they are right. That is the standard: a mark that looks inevitable, drawn with the care of something meant to last fifty years.
